storyteller.name: Storyteller
storyteller.description: Warm, soothing adult storyteller who reads the book and answers the kids' questions

kid_older.name: Leo (Age 8)
kid_older.description: Curious 8-year-old who asks about the plot and loves guessing mysteries

kid_younger.name: Mia (Age 5)
kid_younger.description: Playful 5-year-old who notices funny and cute visual details, giggles and gasps

lines.speaker: storyteller
lines.text: Snuggle in for The Three Little Pigs. Can you use your builder eyes to spot what each pig makes a house from?

lines.speaker: kid_younger
lines.text: <giggle> My builder eyes are wide open!

lines.speaker: storyteller
lines.text: Pip, Poppy, and Pebble set out to build houses. They walked down the same sunny lane so they could live close enough to wave.

lines.speaker: storyteller
lines.text: Pip stacked straw, bundle by bundle. The bundles were light, so by snack time Pip had a house! <chuckle>

lines.speaker: kid_younger
lines.text: See that yellow bundle by the apple? Can you point to what Pip built with? Take your time.

lines.speaker: kid_older
lines.text: <gasp> Pip has a whole house by snack time! Is straw lighter to lift than bricks?

lines.speaker: storyteller
lines.text: There’s the straw, all bundled up. Yes, straw is light to lift, so Pip could stack it quickly. Bricks are heavier.

lines.speaker: storyteller
lines.text: Poppy tied sticks, bundle by bundle. The sticks made a shady roof, so Poppy ate lunch on the doorstep.

lines.speaker: storyteller
lines.text: Pebble laid bricks, one by one. When a brick wobbled, Pebble set it straight.

lines.speaker: storyteller
lines.text: By teatime, even the tallest wall stood steady.

lines.speaker: kid_younger
lines.text: Can you point to the red things in that straight row? What are they called? Take your time.

lines.speaker: kid_older
lines.text: Straw looks floppy. Are bricks sturdier because they don’t bend?

lines.speaker: storyteller
lines.text: Those are bricks. They’re hard and hold their shape. See how Pebble straightened that wobbly brick so the wall would stand steady?

pages.qa_grounding: straight row of warm red bricks

lines.speaker: storyteller
lines.text: Pebble fitted the door, then slid the bolt across. Click!

lines.speaker: storyteller
lines.text: Inside, Pebble set out three cushions so there would be room for everyone.

lines.speaker: storyteller
lines.text: Wolf huffed, and the straw flew up like dry leaves. Scamper, scamper!

lines.speaker: storyteller
lines.text: Pip ran next door, and Poppy opened the door wide. <sigh>

lines.speaker: storyteller
lines.text: Wolf huffed, and the sticks clattered down like wooden spoons. <gasp> Scamper, scamper!

lines.speaker: storyteller
lines.text: Pip and Poppy ran to Pebble, who tucked them inside and slid the bolt. Click!

lines.speaker: kid_younger
lines.text: <sigh> They both got inside. Can you point to what Pebble made the house from? I’ll give you a moment.

lines.speaker: storyteller
lines.text: Those are bricks. Pebble got Pip and Poppy inside and slid the bolt to hold the door shut.

lines.speaker: storyteller
lines.text: Wolf huffed, and the grass bent low. Wolf puffed, and the scarf fluttered.

lines.speaker: storyteller
lines.text: The bricks stayed put, and the three little pigs stayed snug. <sigh>

lines.speaker: storyteller
lines.text: Wolf's cheeks grew tired. The bricks stayed put, so Wolf wrapped up in the scarf and went home.

lines.speaker: storyteller
lines.text: From the window, three little pigs watched Wolf disappear around the bend.

lines.speaker: kid_older
lines.text: Even after all that puffing, the bricks stayed put. How did that keep the pigs safe?

lines.speaker: storyteller
lines.text: The sturdy brick walls held firm, so all three pigs could stay snug inside while Wolf went home.

lines.speaker: storyteller
lines.text: Pip poured the tea, Poppy passed the toast, and Pebble scooted over. Tomorrow they could build together, brick by brick.

lines.speaker: storyteller
lines.text: Tonight there was room for three.

lines.speaker: kid_younger
lines.text: <giggle> Show me the house that kept all three pigs safe!

lines.speaker: kid_older
lines.text: What helped it stay standing? I think those sturdy bricks did the trick!

lines.speaker: storyteller
lines.text: Thanks for building along with us. Subscribe and come back for our next story!
